summary: Facepalm: Facepalm scan for 2026-11-08 (window Nov. 2–8). Most of the fresh blunders found were again about elections. Two candidates met every rule with two accepted publishers, and I checked every quote word for word against the pages I opened. (1) Wallingford, Conn.: poll workers fed about 100 hand-count ballots through a tabulator, which forced a full recount of about 18,000 ballots (NBC Boston, WFSB). (2) The Associated Press says a data-entry error briefly showed a wrong vote total in Florida's 26th Congressional District race (NBC 6 Miami, CBS News Miami). Shasta County, Calif., was a strong third lead, but only one accepted source (CalMatters) was found before the search budget ran out. Both candidates are election stories, close to recent published days; non-election searches (signs, recalls, odd arrests, billing errors) produced nothing in the window with accepted coverage. Genius: Genius scan for 2026-11-08 found no story that meets the two-source rule, so I am submitting no candidates. I ran out of searches before finding a second accepted source for the strongest lead: Montana RB Eli Gillman breaking Cooper Kupp's Big Sky career touchdown record on Nov. 7. The only copy I could open is an AP wire story on abcnews.com, which is not the listed abcnews.go.com domain. I went through the ScienceDaily items from Nov. 4–8. Every U.S. result was either too old by its journal date, an association study, or not from the U.S. Caltech's in-orbit assembly still has only official pages, because Phys.org is still not accessible. No genius story met the standard; nothing published. The verified facepalm story is on the bench for a later day.

candidates.headline: Wallingford, Conn., recounts every Election Day ballot after 100 hand-count ballots go through a tabulator
candidates.reason: passed every check; kept for a later day because the other side had no story

candidates.headline: AP says a data-entry error briefly showed a wrong vote total in Florida's 26th District race
Shasta County, Calif., is the only county in the state still counting in-person ballots after an election-night setup failure
candidates.reason: In the window (Nov. 3–4). CalMatters reports that officials hadn't set up their computer system properly. But CalMatters was the only accepted source opened: other coverage was KRCR, Action News Now, Shasta Scout, Jefferson Public Radio and Yahoo, none of which is accepted. The search budget ran out before an LA Times or Sacramento Bee page could be found. The CalMatters piece also mixes analysis into its reporting.

candidates.headline: Floyd County, Ind., candidate weighs legal options after a commission race was left off 572 early and mail ballots
candidates.reason: The ballot error itself was found and reported in early October, outside the 7-day window. The only new development (Nov. 5) is the narrow result and the candidate's response, and only one accepted source (Louisville Public Media) was opened.

candidates.headline: Tarrant County, Texas, long estimated wait times at some polling places turn out to be inaccurate
candidates.reason: The Dallas Morning News page couldn't be opened, and the only other copy found was on Yahoo (banned). Whether this was a blunder or a data lag isn't established.

candidates.headline: AI agent deletes a Chicago law professor's lecture notes
candidates.reason: This is a private individual's misfortune, not an act whose consequence he brought on himself. The only coverage found was Tom's Hardware, Dexerto and other outlets that aren't accepted.

candidates.headline: Montana RB Eli Gillman breaks Cooper Kupp's Big Sky Conference career total-touchdown record (78) in a 57-24 win over Portland State, Missoula (Nov. 7)
candidates.reason: In the U.S. and inside the window. The only accepted-type page I opened is an AP wire story hosted on abcnews.com, which is not the listed abcnews.go.com domain. The other coverage found (NCAA.com, Yahoo, Skyline Sports, FloFootball, Montana Sports, SWX) is not accepted. I hit the search limit before finding an apnews.com, Missoulian, Billings Gazette or MTPR page. Worth retrying first.

candidates.headline: Ferris State ties the NCAA Division II record with its 40th straight football win, 80-0 over Wayne State (Nov. 7)
candidates.reason: It ties the record rather than breaking it. The only accepted page, from the Detroit News, could not be opened ('url too long'). Yahoo is republishing a WZZM story, and WZZM is not on the list. The other sources are NCAA.com, FloFootball and the Ferris State athletics site, none of which is accepted.

candidates.headline: Brevard College kicker Alex Araneda makes a 63-yard field goal, the longest in NCAA Division III history (Nov. 7)
candidates.reason: The only coverage found was NCAA.com, NCFootballNews and the college's X post. None of them is an accepted publisher.

candidates.headline: Caltech's ASTRA payload autonomously assembles a truss structure in orbit under DARPA's NOM4D program (announced Nov. 5)
candidates.reason: Still only official sources: Caltech's news page and DARPA's page. Phys.org returned 'not accessible' again. The other coverage (Pasadena Now, Knowridge, ana.ir, Ingenieur.de, KultureGeek, Geek Slop) is not accepted.

candidates.headline: MIT nanoparticles engineer CAR natural killer cells inside the body in mice (Nature Biotechnology)
candidates.reason: Too old. The Nature page metadata gives an online date of Oct. 13, 2026, and ScienceDaily's Nov. 8 page is a repost. It is also a mouse study.

candidates.headline: Record-intensity 300-attosecond hard X-ray pulses (Optica)
candidates.reason: Not in the U.S. The experiment ran at the European XFEL in Germany, the first author is from the University of Tokyo, and the experiment took place in April 2026.

candidates.headline: Electrons tracked at a 'space-time limit' with ultrafast microscopy (Nature Photonics)
candidates.reason: Not in the U.S. The work is from the University of Regensburg and the Max Planck Institute in Hamburg, and the paper is in vol. 20, issue 8, an earlier issue.

candidates.headline: Luka Doncic averages 40+ points through the season's first nine games, matching Wilt Chamberlain (Nov. 6)
candidates.reason: A narrow statistical combination rather than a distinct record. The only sources seen were NBA.com and Yahoo, neither of which is accepted.

candidates.headline: UTHealth Houston study links high-dose flu shots to lower Alzheimer's risk (Neurology)
candidates.reason: An observational association study rather than an achievement. It is in Neurology vol. 106, issue 8, so the publication date is not confirmed inside the window, and the only accepted source is a ScienceDaily repost.

candidates.headline: Other ScienceDaily items Nov. 6–8: white-dwarf double debris disc, Mars HCl signals
candidates.reason: Not in the U.S. The sources are the European Southern Observatory and the European Space Agency, and both findings are hedged.
